q: Had I known about the storm, I ___ the trip.
explain: Inverted third conditional: Had I known… = If I had known…, would have + p.p.

q: The bridge is thought ___ over 500 years ago.
explain: Passive reporting about the past: is thought + to have been + p.p.

q: I'd rather you ___ tell anyone.
explain: would rather + someone + past simple for present/future preferences.

q: She denied ___ the crystal.
explain: deny + -ing.

q: By next summer, they ___ the new castle.
explain: Future perfect: completed before a future time.

q: It's high time we ___ home.
explain: It's (high) time + past simple.

q: The swans, ___ feathers shimmered, glided past.
explain: 'whose' shows possession.

q: He must ___ the wrong path; he's still not here.
explain: must have + p.p. = deduction about the past.

q: I'm not used to ___ so much attention.
explain: be used to + -ing.

q: She'd have won the race if she ___ fallen.
explain: Third conditional: if + past perfect.

q: ___ by the long journey, the knight fell asleep.
explain: Past participle clause = 'Because he was exhausted…'

q: You ___ have brought a gift, but it's very kind of you.
explain: needn't have + p.p. = you did it, but it wasn't necessary.

q: She's one of the few people ___ can solve the riddle.
explain: 'who' as subject for people.

q: I regret ___ you that the boat has sunk.
explain: regret to tell/inform = formal bad news now; regret telling = sorry about the past.

q: The more you practise, ___ you become.
explain: the + comparative…, the + comparative.

q: Not until the lake froze ___ how cold it was.
explain: After 'Not until…' at the start, invert: did we realise.

q: Whatever happens, we ___ to the plan.
explain: Real future: will + verb.

q: If she hadn't missed the ferry, she ___ here by now.
explain: Mixed conditional: past condition (had missed) → present result (would be).

q: The results ___ until next week.
explain: Future passive: will (not) be + past participle.

q: I wish you ___ interrupting me!
explain: wish + would for annoying behaviour you want to change.

q: He's believed ___ abroad last year.
explain: Passive reporting about the past: is believed + to have + past participle.

q: ___ the map more carefully, we wouldn't have got lost.
explain: Inverted third conditional: Had + subject + past participle.

q: She insisted ___ for the meal.
explain: insist on + -ing.

q: By the time you get this letter, I ___ the mountains.
explain: Future perfect: an action completed before a future time.

q: They had the old tower ___ last spring.
explain: Causative: have + object + past participle.

q: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the tickets.
explain: Negative inversion after 'Not only'.

q: You needn't ___ me a lift; I could have walked.
explain: needn't have + past participle = it was done but wasn't necessary.

q: There's no point ___ about it now.
explain: There's no point (in) + -ing.

q: The guide, ___ we'd met the day before, showed us a shortcut.
explain: 'whom' as the object in a non-defining relative clause.

q: Supposing you ___ the lottery, what would you do?
explain: Supposing (= imagine if) + past simple for an imaginary present/future.

q: It's no use ___ to him; he never listens.
explain: It's no use + -ing.
